c3r.summary: From the conclave of 1549-50. A courier back from the imperial court is said to bring the Emperor's consent to Monte (or Santa Croce) as Pope, a scheme helped by the Duke of Florence. Muzio thinks the news true but does not expect the scheme to succeed, and does not see how the Imperialists would vote for Monte. Del Monte was elected Julius III on 7 Feb 1550.
c3r.en:
Same holes as readingc3r.md: [?...] = value proposed from context only; [13], [24] = code group with no value; [Cardinal], [Your Excellency] = code group whose value the c. 5v margin gives. Emended words are marked in the Italian.

A courier of [13] has come back from the court, who, it is understood, was sent to beg [?His Majesty] to be content that [?either] Santa Croce or Monte be made Pope; and that this scheme has been helped by the [?Duke of] Florence. This man seems to have brought word that [?His Majesty] is content with Monte. As this news seems to me to matter to [Your Excellency], I did not want to delay in giving you notice of it. The Prior of [24] told me this, squaring it with what I write to you, in another letter of mine that comes with this one, about the note of the [Cardinal] de' Medici. I come to think it must be true.

c5.summary: Mostly clear. The cipher reports talk from the conclave: Ferrante and Don Diego had backed Salviati; the Dukes of Florence and Alba disclosed it to the Emperor; Salviati was excluded and Don Diego drew back. In clear, Muzio argues that the candidate Ferrante favours is the fittest in the college.
c5.en:
Same marks and holes as readingc5.md. ⟦ ... ⟧ = deciphered from cipher.

Most Illustrious and Most Excellent Lord,

I wrote two letters to Your Excellency yesterday, and because I wrote so briefly of having spoken with the lord Don Diego, I now say again that I tried to make sure whether the news I had been told was true, and I recalled Your Excellency's interest. He answered that the news was not true, and that nothing would be left undone so that no such harm should be done to Your Excellency.

From the conclave come various reports, which agree in this sense: that ⟦[Your Excellency] and [?Don Diego] had taken up the protection of Salviati, and (?) in order to become by that favour, the one [?Duke of] Milan, and [?Don Diego] master of Siena (?); that the [?Duke of] Florence and the [?Duke of] Alba have disclosed this scheme to [?His Majesty].

snip.cap: Muzio to Ferrante Gonzaga, 11 January 1550: the first four cipher lines of c. 3r

system: Simple substitution on letter-like signs and single digits, with two signs each for a, e, i, o, u and s, separate signs for doubled letters, four digit-pair nulls and one stop-null, and a small code of number groups and one sign for titles and persons.
